plannedTimeline.detail: Downtown Oceanside, Mission Ave near the pier. Walk from the car. Confirm the pin on their site.

plannedTimeline.title: Piper (at Seabird)
plannedTimeline.detail: Coastal California cooking. Breakfast daily 7-11am. Fuel up - it's a riding day.

plannedTimeline.title: Rancho Del Oro · 8 homes, close together
plannedTimeline.detail: In person with Nick: 8 homes in about 2.5 hours, all close together in Rancho Del Oro / Ivey Ranch. If it wraps with time left, the self-guided pockets are still Loma Alta (established, close to downtown) and Mira Costa (quieter streets, ~10 min to the beach). 🗺️ Bike route

plannedTimeline.title: Tanner's Prime Burgers
plannedTimeline.detail: Vista Way, Oceanside - the lunch after the Rancho Del Oro tour, then back toward the pier. Downtown alt: 333 Pacific, or fish tacos by the pier.

plannedTimeline.title: Oceanside Pier & The Strand
plannedTimeline.detail: Walk the pier out and back (bikes aren't for the pier deck), then roll The Strand south.

plannedTimeline.title: Revolution Roasters - Oceanside
plannedTimeline.detail: S Coast Hwy. House-roasted, community café. Open daily 6am-6pm.

plannedTimeline.title: 4th Oceanside home, then Trader Joe's (2570 Vista Way)
plannedTimeline.detail: Ride to the last door, time the walk to the nearest park, then a TJ's aisle walk - fold the Brompton into a cart or lock it out front. Is this your weekly rhythm? Alt: Sprouts · College Blvd.

plannedTimeline.title: Oceanside Harbor
plannedTimeline.detail: Boat life. Easy flat roll north from the pier along The Strand / Pacific St, loop Harbor Village, back for the market. 🗺️ Bike route

plannedTimeline.title: Oceanside Sunset Market
plannedTimeline.detail: Pier View Way, downtown. Thursday evenings: food stalls, music, vendors. Bike back in the boot first, then walk it. Confirm hours. Sit-down alts: Anita's Mexican (the South Coast Highway location, not the other one), or The Switchboard - Fin Hotel.

plannedTimeline.detail: Send the day's photos before you forget which door was which. 🗺️ Maps drive · Oceanside → Vista

notes.summary: In-person tour with Nick (Compass) through Rancho Del Oro, Oceanside. The notes describe 8 homes in about 2.5 hours, all close together. John's showing schedule has 9 Oceanside addresses. View, privacy (no one looking in), and outdoor space came first. A good kitchen matters to Maya. Also wanted: a walk-in closet, and a fourth flex room for an office or playroom. Solar and a vegetable garden are nice-to-haves. A gated community is preferred, and a cul-de-sac or quiet street is strongly preferred.
highlights: Top three: view, privacy, and outdoor space.
A good kitchen matters to Maya. A walk-in closet. A fourth flex room for an office or playroom.
Nice-to-haves: solar and a vegetable garden. Gated community preferred. Cul-de-sac or a quiet street, strongly.
Windows: check for fog and age. A full-house replacement is about $25-30K.
A tankless water heater is ideal. An old unit is about $1,500 to replace.
Read solar lease contracts carefully. Some are predatory.
HOA on this tour ran about $140-200/mo. Confirm what that fee covers.
Single-family homes under $1M are getting hard to find. The market is a bit frozen, so buyers have more room on price.
Nick's tip: put the MLS photos into Claude and ask it to decorate them for layout ideas.
The showing schedule has 9 stops. 1861 Avenida Segovia was on it and had no tour writeup.
nextSteps: Friday with Nick, 1:00-3:00 PM: 6 homes in Carlsbad and Shadowridge.

takeaway: 1242 Via Candelas was the standout: the view, nobody behind the house, and a gated community, with a known list of floors, garden, and kitchen cosmetics. The other houses in the notes did not beat that mix. The schedule had nine stops, and 1861 Avenida Segovia had no tour notes.
